candidates.label: gameServer

candidates.label: legalName

candidates.label: underName

candidates.label: additionalName

candidates.label: name

candidates.label: characterName
candidates.comment: A naming relation for a performance role, indicating the name of the character being played. Also called "role name", "played character", "fictional name". candidates.label: busName

candidates.label: roleName
candidates.comment: The specific designation or title of a role performed by a person or organization. Also called role title, position name, function name. Examples: `Person in Movie` roleName `"Actor"`, `Team Member` roleName `"Quarterback"`, `Project Contributor` roleName `"Lead Developer"`.

candidates.label: callSign
candidates.comment: An identification relation between a broadcast service, person, or vehicle and its unique callsign. Also called "radio identifier", "station ID", "vehicle identifier". candidates.label: identifier
candidates.comment: An identifier relation between any thing and a unique identifier for it. Also called ID, unique ID, reference number, code. Examples: "A product has an identifier 'GTIN123'.", "A person has an identifier 'UUID-XYZ'.", "This thing has an identifier URL."

chosen_property.definition: Indicates what an event or period commemorates.

candidates.label: occurredDuring
candidates.comment: The subject event or observation occurred within the specified time period or concurrent with another event.

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: startTime
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning time of an action, reservation, or media segment. Also called "beginning time", "commencement time", "start of action", "reservation time". Examples: "The reservation has startTime 7:00 PM", "The action's startTime was 10:30 AM", "The media clip's startTime is 00:01:15.". candidates.label: recordedAt
candidates.comment: A recording location relation between a creative work and the event where it was recorded. Also called recorded during, captured at event. Examples: "A live album was recorded at 'Wembley Stadium Concert'.", "A documentary film was recorded at 'the Amazon Rainforest Expedition'.", "A podcast episode was recorded at 'a conference panel discussion'.". Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. Also called "event time", "depicted time", "time of content". Examples: "News article contentReferenceTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00Z'", "Historical documentary contentReferenceTime '1945-09-02'".

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: duration
candidates.comment: A duration relation between an item (such as an event, media object, or schedule) and its length of time. Also called "length", "time span", "period". Examples: "Movie 'Avatar' duration 'PT2H42M'", "Event 'Concert' duration 'PT3H'", "Audio recording duration 'PT5M30S'". Distinct from durationOfWarranty, which is specifically about warranty length.

candidates.label: name
candidates.comment: A name or title identifying a thing. Also called title, designation, appellation, label. Examples: "Book name 'The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy'", "Person name 'Alice Smith'", "Company name 'Acme Corp'". Distinct from alternateName, which is an alias or alternative name.

chosen_property.definition: Indicates the purpose or beneficiary of something.

candidates.label: beneficiaryBank
candidates.comment: A bank, branch, or financial institution operating the beneficiary's bank account or releasing funds for a money transfer. Examples: "MoneyTransfer 'Wire Transfer' beneficiaryBank 'Bank of America'", "MoneyTransfer 'International Transfer' beneficiaryBank 'HSBC'."

candidates.label: sponsor
candidates.comment: A support relation between an entity (creative work, event, grant, study, organization, or person) and the person or organization providing financial or other backing. Examples: "The event has sponsor Acme Corp", "The medical study's sponsor is the NIH", "This artist has sponsor a private foundation."

candidates.label: isGift
candidates.comment: A transaction intent relation indicating whether an order was placed as a gift for a recipient other than the buyer. Also called gift purchase, purchased as gift, gift order. Examples: An order has isGift set to 'true'. A purchase has isGift set to 'false'. A book order has isGift set to 'true' with gift wrapping.

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: worksFor
candidates.comment: An employment relation between a person and an organization, indicating the organization for which the person is employed. Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.

candidates.label: governmentBenefitsInfo
candidates.comment: A government benefits info relation between a special announcement and information about associated government services or benefits. Also called: public aid details, government assistance, benefit programs. Examples: "Pandemic Relief Announcement" government benefits info "Unemployment Benefits Program", "Housing Crisis Alert" government benefits info "Rental Assistance Program", "Disaster Recovery Notice" government benefits info "FEMA Aid Services".

candidates.label: hasTierBenefit
candidates.comment: A tier benefit relation between a member program tier and a specific benefit associated with that tier. Also called tier advantage, member perk, program benefit. candidates.label: businessFunction
candidates.comment: A characterization of the business function associated with a demand, offer, or component of a bundle. Also called "purpose of offer", "transaction type", "commercial role". candidates.label: seeks
candidates.comment: A demand for specific products or services expressed by an organization or person. Also called desires, looks for, requests, requires. Examples: `Company X` seeks `Demand for Software Developers`, `Person Y` seeks `Demand for Used Car`, `Organization Z` seeks `Demand for Consulting Services`. Distinct from `offers`, which is about what is provided.

candidates.label: recipient
candidates.comment: A recipient relation between an action (like sending or paying) and the audience, contact point, organization, or person receiving it. Also called receiver, intended for, sent to. candidates.label: producer
candidates.comment: A creative role relation between a creative work and the person or organization responsible for its production. Also called production company, executive producer, creator, maker. Examples: A movie has a producer 'Steven Spielberg'. A music album has a producer 'Universal Music Group'. A TV series has a producer 'Shonda Rhimes'. candidates.label: broadcaster
candidates.comment: An ownership or operational relation between a broadcast service and the organization responsible for it. Also called "service provider", "operated by", "owned by", "broadcast by". Examples: "BBC Radio 4 broadcaster BBC", "CNN broadcast service broadcaster Warner Bros. Discovery".

candidates.label: produces
candidates.comment: An outcome relation between a service and the tangible thing it generates or provides. Also called generates, yields, creates, provides. Examples: A government service produces a 'passport'. A licensing service produces a 'permit'. A printing service produces 'documents'.

candidates.label: manufacturer
candidates.comment: A manufacturing relation between a product and the organization that produced it. Also called: produced by, made by, fabricated by. Examples: "Smartphone manufacturer Apple", "Automobile manufacturer Toyota", "Furniture manufacturer IKEA".

candidates.label: productionCompany
candidates.comment: A production relation between a creative work (like a movie or series) and the organization responsible for its creation. Also called produced by, studio, made by, created by. Examples: "The movie 'Dune' was produced by Legendary Pictures.", "The TV series 'The Crown' was produced by Left Bank Pictures.", "The video game 'Cyberpunk 2077' was produced by CD Projekt Red."

candidates.label: hasParticipationOffer
candidates.comment: A participation offer relation between an event and an offer to participate in it. Also called call for participation, participation opportunity, event entry offer. candidates.label: publisher
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a creative work or financial incentive and the organization or person that publishes it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. candidates.label: productionDate
candidates.comment: A production date relation between a product or vehicle and the specific date it was manufactured. Also called manufactured on, made on, creation date. Examples: "A 2023 Toyota Camry has a production date of 2022-11-15.", "A vintage car has a production date of 1965-03-01.", "A smartphone has a production date of 2024-01-20."

candidates.label: creator
candidates.comment: An authorship relation between a creative work or user comment and the person or organization responsible for its creation. Also called: author, originator, producer, made by. candidates.label: hasRepresentation

candidates.label: brand

candidates.label: hasRepresentation
candidates.comment: A representation relation between a biochemical entity and its common symbolic or structural representation. Also called represented by, symbolic form, structural representation. candidates.label: hasPOS

candidates.label: targetPlatform

candidates.label: contentType

candidates.label: discussionUrl

candidates.label: events

candidates.label: articleSection

Also called enacted work, live presentation, staged work. Examples: TheaterEvent workPerformed "Hamlet", ConcertEvent workPerformed "Symphony No. 5", DancePerformance workPerformed "Swan Lake". Distinct from workFeatured, which is a general showcasing, and workPresented, which is specifically for movies at screening events.

candidates.label: artEdition
candidates.comment: A numerical or textual description of the total number of copies produced for a piece of visual artwork. Also called: edition size, print run, limited edition count. Examples: "VisualArtwork 'Sunset' artEdition '20'", "VisualArtwork 'Lithograph' artEdition '1/50'", "VisualArtwork 'Sculpture' artEdition 'Unique'."

candidates.label: artist
candidates.comment: A person who is the primary creator of a comic issue, comic story, or visual artwork, especially in non-line art mediums. Also called: creator, illustrator, visual creator. Examples: "VisualArtwork 'Starry Night' artist 'Vincent van Gogh'", "ComicIssue 'Issue #1' artist 'Frank Miller'", "ComicStory 'Origin Story' artist 'Alex Ross'". Distinct from author, which is a more general term for the creator of content, often textual.

relations.embedding_query_text: performed on: Indicates the type of tour or performance context.

chosen_property.label: performedOn
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the type of tour or performance context.
chosen_property.justification: No existing property directly captures the 'performed on' relationship for a performance context. 'performerIn' is a suitable super-property.

candidates.label: firstPerformance
candidates.comment: A first performance relation between a music composition and the event where it was initially performed. Also called: premiere, debut performance, initial staging. Examples: "Beethoven's 5th Symphony" first performance "Vienna, 1808 Concert", "Hamilton Musical" first performance "Public Theater, NYC 2015", "New Opera 'The Siren'" first performance "Royal Opera House Gala".

candidates.label: byArtist
candidates.comment: A performance relation between a music album or recording and the music group or person who performed it. Also called "performed by", "artist of", "featuring artist". Examples: "Album 'Thriller' byArtist Michael Jackson", "Recording 'Bohemian Rhapsody' byArtist Queen". Distinct from composer, which is the person who wrote the music, whereas byArtist is the performer.

candidates.label: performer
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and an organization or person who performs at it. Also called artist, entertainer, presenter, actor. Examples: A concert has a performer 'Taylor Swift'. A play has a performer 'Meryl Streep'. A conference has a performer 'Dr. Jane Doe'. Distinct from performerIn, which points from a person to an event.

candidates.label: entertainmentBusiness
candidates.comment: An entertainment business relation between a perform action and the entertainment business where the action occurred. Also called "venue", "performance location", "showplace". Examples: "Perform action entertainmentBusiness 'Concert Hall'", "Perform action entertainmentBusiness 'Theater Royal'", "Perform action entertainmentBusiness 'Comedy Club'". Distinct from location, which is a more general property for any place an action occurs.

candidates.label: performers
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and its primary performers, who can be organizations or persons. Also called main artists, headliners, principal actors, featured performers. Examples: A concert has performers 'Coldplay'. A play has performers 'The Royal Shakespeare Company'. A festival has performers 'Various Artists'. Distinct from performer, which can be any performer, not necessarily the main one.

candidates.label: recordedAt
candidates.comment: A recording location relation between a creative work and the event where it was recorded. Also called recorded during, captured at event. Examples: "A live album was recorded at 'Wembley Stadium Concert'.", "A documentary film was recorded at 'the Amazon Rainforest Expedition'.", "A podcast episode was recorded at 'a conference panel discussion'.". Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: displayLocation
candidates.comment: A display location relation between a creative work or product and the place where it can be viewed or experienced in-person. Also called "viewing location", "exhibition place", "experience venue". Examples: "Painting 'Mona Lisa' displayLocation 'Louvre Museum'", "Product 'New Car Model' displayLocation 'Dealership Showroom'", "Sculpture displayLocation 'Art Gallery'".

candidates.label: performerIn
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between a person and an event in which they perform or participate. Also called performs in, participates in, acts in, presents at. Examples: John Doe is a performer in 'The Annual Gala'. Jane Smith is a performer in 'The City Marathon'. An actor is a performer in 'The New Play'. Distinct from performer, which points from an event to a person.

candidates.label: howPerformed
candidates.comment: A performance method relation between a medical procedure and a description of how it is carried out. Also called procedure steps, method of procedure, execution details. Examples: "A medical procedure has a description of how it is performed.", "The surgery details how it is performed.", "This procedure outlines how it is performed."

candidates.label: sportsActivityLocation

Also called "exercise location", "training venue", "athletic facility", "gym location". relations.relation_phrase: forced to shut down due to
relations.definition: Indicates the reason an organization was forced to cease operations.
relations.embedding_query_text: forced to shut down due to: Indicates the reason an organization was forced to cease operations.

chosen_property.label: forcedToShutDownDueTo
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the reason an organization was forced to cease operations.
chosen_property.justification: No existing property directly captures the specific 'forced to shut down due to' relationship. 'cause' is a suitable super-property.

candidates.label: dissolutionDate
candidates.comment: A dissolution date relation between an organization and the date when it was dissolved. Also called "closure date", "ceased operations date", "disbandment date". Examples: "Company 'Acme Corp' dissolutionDate '2023-01-15'", "Non-profit organization dissolutionDate '2022-07-01'", "Partnership dissolutionDate '2024-03-10'".

candidates.label: closes
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for opening hours, indicating the closing time for a place or service on a given day. Also called "closing time", "end of hours", "closes at". Examples: "Store opening hours closes '18:00'", "Service opening hours closes '22:30'". Distinct from opens, which specifies the opening time.

candidates.label: availableThrough
candidates.comment: A date and time after which an item will no longer be available for pickup. Also called: pickup end time, collection deadline. Examples: "DeliveryEvent 'Package' availableThrough '2023-10-30T17:00:00'", "DeliveryEvent 'Order' availableThrough '2023-11-01'". Distinct from availableFrom, which specifies the start of pickup availability.

candidates.label: conditionsOfAccess
candidates.comment: A descriptive relation for a creative work, detailing the natural language conditions affecting its availability or access methods. Also called "access restrictions", "availability terms", "usage conditions". Examples: "Archival document conditionsOfAccess 'Available by appointment only'", "Digital artwork conditionsOfAccess 'Requires institutional login'".

candidates.label: schoolClosuresInfo
candidates.comment: Information regarding school closures, typically provided as a URL or web content within a special announcement. Also called school closing details, closure announcement, education disruption info. Examples: `Emergency Announcement` schoolClosuresInfo `URL to district website`, `Weather Alert` schoolClosuresInfo `Text about snow day`, `Public Health Notice` schoolClosuresInfo `WebContent on school status`.

candidates.label: publicTransportClosuresInfo
candidates.comment: A public transport closures information relation between a special announcement and details regarding public transport disruptions. Also called transport closure details, public transit alerts. Examples: "A special announcement includes public transport closures info about subway lines.", "An emergency alert provides public transport closures info for bus routes.", "A news update contains public transport closures info for train services."

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: archiveHeld
candidates.comment: An archive held relation between an archive organization and a collection, fonds, or item maintained by it. Also called archival holding, collection maintained, item preserved. Examples: "The National Archives' archive held is 'Presidential Papers'.", "The historical society's archive held is 'Local Family Records'."

candidates.label: serviceOperator
candidates.comment: The organization responsible for operating a government service, distinct from the primary provider. Also called service management, operating entity, service subcontractor. Examples: `Public Transport Service` serviceOperator `Transit Authority`, `Waste Collection Service` serviceOperator `Private Waste Management Company`, `National Park Service` serviceOperator `Local Park Management`. Distinct from `provider`, which is the primary organization offering the service.

candidates.label: requiresSubscription
candidates.comment: A subscription requirement relation indicating whether an action access or media object necessitates a subscription for use. Also called subscription needed, paywall, access restriction. Examples: "A streaming movie requires subscription 'true'.", "A news article requires subscription 'false'.", "A premium feature requires subscription 'true'."

relations.definition: Indicates the date on which a publication was released.
relations.embedding_query_text: is publication date of: Indicates the date on which a publication was released.

chosen_property.label: datePublished
chosen_property.justification: The 'datePublished' property, when inverted, indicates that the date is the publication date of the URL (representing a creative work).

candidates.label: datePublished
candidates.comment: A temporal release relation between a certification or creative work and its date of first publication or broadcast. Also called: publication date, broadcast date, release date. Examples: "Book" date published "1984-06-08", "TV Show Episode" date published "2023-01-01", "Certification" date published "2022-12-01". Distinct from dateCreated, which is the date of creation, and datePosted, which is for online listings.

candidates.label: releaseDate
candidates.comment: A release date relation between a product and the date it was made available to the public. Also called launch date, availability date, publication date. Examples: "A new smartphone model has a release date of 2024-03-01.", "A software update has a release date of 2023-11-15.", "A new car model has a release date of 2025-01-01.". Distinct from productionDate, which is when the item was manufactured.

candidates.label: datePosted
candidates.comment: A temporal publication relation between a CDCPMD record, job posting, real estate listing, or special announcement and its online publication date. Also called: posting date, publication date, listing date. Examples: "Job Opening" date posted "2023-10-25", "Apartment for Rent" date posted "2023-10-20", "Public Health Alert" date posted "2023-03-01T09:00:00Z". Distinct from datePublished, which is a more general property for first publication.

candidates.label: sdDatePublished
candidates.comment: The date when the structured data associated with a creative work was generated or published. Also called structured data publication date, metadata publish date, data generation date. Examples: `Article JSON-LD` sdDatePublished `2023-10-26`, `Recipe Structured Data` sdDatePublished `2023-09-15`, `Event Markup` sdDatePublished `2023-08-01`. Distinct from `datePublished`, which is the publication date of the creative work itself.

candidates.label: publication
candidates.comment: A publication relation between a creative work and the event of its publication. Also called published as, associated publication event. Examples: "A book has a publication event in 2023.", "A research paper has a publication event in a journal.", "A song has a publication event as a single."

candidates.label: publishedBy
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a publication event and the organization or person responsible for it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book's publication event was published by 'Penguin Random House'.", "A journal article's publication event was published by 'Elsevier'.", "A blog post's publication event was published by 'Jane Doe'.". Distinct from publisher, which refers to the publisher of the creative work itself.

candidates.label: releasedEvent
candidates.comment: A released event relation between a creative work and the publication event marking its release. Also called release event, launch event. Examples: "A movie has a released event 'Premiere at Cannes Film Festival'.", "A book has a released event 'Book Launch Party'.", "A video game has a released event 'E3 Announcement'."

candidates.label: releaseOf
candidates.comment: A release of relation between a music release and the music album it originates from. Also called part of album, from album. Examples: "A music release 'Single A' is a release of 'Album X'.", "A digital track is a release of 'The Greatest Hits Album'.", "A vinyl edition is a release of 'Classic Rock Album'."

candidates.label: guidelineDate
candidates.comment: A guideline date relation between a medical guideline and the date its recommendations were issued. Also called: recommendation date, issue date, publication date. Examples: "AHA Guideline for Hypertension" guideline date "2017-11-13", "NICE Guideline for Diabetes" guideline date "2020-08-19", "WHO COVID-19 Guidelines" guideline date "2023-03-01".

candidates.label: productionDate
candidates.comment: A production date relation between a product or vehicle and the specific date it was manufactured. Also called manufactured on, made on, creation date. Examples: "A 2023 Toyota Camry has a production date of 2022-11-15.", "A vintage car has a production date of 1965-03-01.", "A smartphone has a production date of 2024-01-20."
